items.title: Factory AI $150M Series C: $1.5B Khosla Bet [2026] - tech-insider.org
sentences: Factory AI $150M Series C: $1.5B Khosla Bet [2026]

Factory, the San Francisco-based startup building autonomous AI agents for enterprise engineering teams, announced on April 16, 2026, that it has closed a $150 million Series C funding round at a $1.5 billion post-money valuation .

The round, led by Khosla Ventures with participation from Sequoia Capital, Insight Partners, Blackstone, Evantic Capital, 20VC, NEA, and Mantis VC, officially launched the three-year-old company into unicorn territory – and it proved to be just the opening chapter: by August 2026, Factory’s total disclosed funding had climbed to roughly $326.74 million across rounds, according to data from Forge Global, reshaping the competitive landscape of AI coding tools aimed at Fortune 500 developers.

With revenue reportedly doubling every month over the past six months and customers ranging from Nvidia to Morgan Stanley, Factory’s Series C signals that enterprise buyers are finally ready to pay for autonomous coding at scale.
Factory AI Funding Round Details and Investor Lineup
The Series C round closed at exactly $150 million, valuing Factory at $1.5 billion on a post-money basis.
Khosla Ventures, led by managing director Keith Rabois – who joined Factory’s board as part of the transaction – served as the lead investor and anchored the deal.
The round also attracted Evantic Capital, 20VC (Harry Stebbings’ fund), NEA, Mantis VC, and Abstract Ventures.

Just three months later, Factory returned to market: according to Forge Global secondary-market data, the company closed a follow-on Series C-2 of $120 million in July 2026 at a $4 billion valuation, more than doubling its worth in a single fundraising cycle.

The company’s capital efficiency, previously tracked at 4.29x during its July 2025 round, was cited by multiple investors as a key reason for the aggressive valuation step-up from a reported $300 million valuation less than ten months earlier – a fivefold increase driven almost entirely by revenue growth and enterprise retention data, and one that continued into the following quarter: by July 2026 Factory’s valuation had reached $4 billion on the back of its Series C-2, pushing cumulative disclosed funding to approximately $326.74 million by August 2026, per Forge Global.
“This puts Factory’s valuation at $1.5 billion and will accelerate our investment in research, product, and global go-to-market,” Grinberg wrote in the company’s blog post announcing the round.
Factory’s Series C arrives in the middle of the most heavily funded year in AI coding history.
